Bubble and Squeak

Served at: St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

Serves 4-6Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Bubble and Squeak is a beloved British dish, traditionally made on St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day) with the delicious leftovers from Christmas dinner. It's a comforting, crispy pan-fried patty of mashed potatoes and cooked cabbage or other greens, offering a delightful second act to your holiday feast.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (approx. 900g) leftover mashed potatoes
  • 2 cups (approx. 300g) cooked cabbage, Brussels sprouts, or other greens, finely chopped
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) vegetable oil or butter, plus more for frying
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • Optional: 1/2 cup (75g) cooked chopped ham or turkey

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the leftover mashed potatoes and finely chopped cooked cabbage (or other greens). If using, add any cooked chopped ham or turkey.
  2. Season the mixture with salt and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until all ingredients are well combined.
  3. Heat 2 tablespoons (30ml) of vegetable oil or butter in a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat.
  4. Carefully spoon the potato and vegetable mixture into the hot pan, pressing it down gently to form a large, flat cake, or divide it into individual patties.
  5. Cook for 8-10 minutes on one side, until a golden-brown, crispy crust forms. Do not disturb too much during this time to allow the crust to develop.
  6. Carefully flip the cake or patties. Add a little more oil or butter to the pan if needed.
  7. Cook for another 8-10 minutes on the second side, until golden brown and heated through.
  8. Remove from the pan and serve hot.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, you can sauté a finely chopped onion with the oil before adding the potato mixture.
  • Serve with leftover gravy, a fried egg, or alongside cold cuts for a complete Boxing Day meal.
  • Ensure your mashed potatoes aren't too wet; if they are, you might want to add a tablespoon or two of flour to help bind the mixture.
